verdict.rationale: Logseq's docs support the story: it markets itself as a 'privacy-first' local knowledge base with markdown-based journals/pages, block/page references, and export to plain Markdown (logseq-docs-23, logseq-docs-1/2/24, logseq-docs-8). However, hands-on community reports directly contradict the 'local files I own' guarantee for the newer DB version, stating the new database format means data can no longer be kept as markdown files (logseq-comm-7), and others note generated markdown isn't cleanly portable to other tools due to formatting quirks (logseq-comm-16), plus historical data-loss concerns (logseq-comm-1). Missing for 10: explicit first-party confirmation that the DB-version graphs remain plain-text/local-file-readable, and independent verification that offline mode has no functional gaps.
